implementation_notes: Closures in Rust capture either by reference (& or &mut) or by move. The borrow checker is the pattern's strongest safety net: a closure that captures &mut state and is returned from a function will not compile unless the state is moved in, which removes the dangling-capture bug C++ has. The Fn/FnMut/FnOnce trait hierarchy encodes exactly how a closure uses its captures, and the common failure - returning a closure that outlives a local borrow - is a compile error rather than undefined behaviour. Closures must be 'static to cross a thread boundary, which is why thread closures almost always need move.
idiom_name: closure with borrow or move capture; Fn / FnMut / FnOnce bound
pitfalls: Returning a closure that borrows a local fails to compile - that is the borrow checker catching a dangling capture; fix it by moving the state or by taking an owned handle.
A closure passed to std::thread::spawn must be 'static, so every borrowed input must be moved or replaced by an Arc.
Fn vs FnMut vs FnOnce is inferred from how the closure uses captures; boxing one to erase the distinction costs an allocation per call.
Closures do not implement Debug, so wrapping them in a struct for logging requires naming the type explicitly.
